steps.action: drop rows whose value is not one of the canonical spellings
steps.reason: a keystroke slip or a clipped word is not a category of its own, and there is no damaged cell here to repair back to -- these rows are, almost always, cars the spine draw never selected

steps.column: year, mileage, tax, mpg, engineSize, paintQuality%, previousOwners, price
steps.action: drop rows holding a value the column's own domain forbids; a missing value is left alone
steps.reason: a negative distance or a fractional owner cannot be repaired without inventing the number, while an empty cell is unknown rather than wrong and is filled later, inside a training fold

steps.action: drop the union of the two rules above
steps.reason: measured against repairing the spellings, dropping costs 19.34 EUR of mean absolute error, nearly seven standard errors and 19 of 20 splits; it is recorded here because this file is indexed positionally by every later week, so its length is fixed, and the cost of that is a number rather than an assertion

steps.action: missing values LEFT OPEN; the 'KNN (k=5) / own level' plan goes to later weeks
steps.reason: a fill computed here would be computed over the rows each later week holds out to score on, so the file would carry a value derived from its own test set; the plan beat the training median by 37.22 EUR on 19 of 20 splits, and each week applies it inside its own split, with KNN on standardised numeric columns

steps.action: outlier treatment: log1p, and log1p on nothing else
steps.reason: the 1.5*IQR rule removes 29.43% of the file, 1,043 rows on tax alone, and what it deletes is the cheap end of the market and the hybrids rather than errors; log1p compresses the long tails of mpg and mileage instead of deleting those cars, and it fits nothing, so each later week applies it inside its own split

measured over twenty splits, the four candidates agree on MAE to within 2.62 EUR against a standard error of about 29, because ordinary least squares on a full-rank design is scale-invariant in fit; cond(X) does fall from 4.456e+07 to 12.75, which is a fact about the solve and not about the score, and a model that is not scale-invariant has to measure this again for itself
